tests.title: normal sentences English and Korean
tests.procedure: sentence_stats('Hello world. How are you?'); sentence_stats('One two three!'); sentence_stats('안녕 하세요. 반갑 습니다 정말!')
tests.expected: (2, 2.5); (1, 3.0); (2, 2.5). Each result is a tuple of (int, float).

tests.title: empty, whitespace-only and punctuation-only text
tests.expected: Every call returns (0, 0.0); the second value is an instance of float.

tests.title: consecutive terminators, unterminated tail, no terminator, mid-sentence period
tests.procedure: sentence_stats('Wow!! Really?! Yes.'); sentence_stats('Hi there. unfinished words'); sentence_stats('hello world'); sentence_stats('Pi is 3.14 ok.')
tests.expected: (3, 1.0); (1, 2.0); (0, 0.0); (2, 2.5) because the period in 3.14 ends a sentence (known limitation ASM-004): 'Pi is 3' has 3 words, '14 ok' has 2.

tests.title: REQ-001 acceptance scenarios
tests.procedure: Import sentence_stats from textstats and call it with: 'Hello world. How are you?'; 'One two three!'; 'Wow!! Really?! Yes.'; '안녕 하세요. 반갑 습니다 정말!'; 'Hi there. unfinished words'

tests.title: REQ-002 and REQ-003 acceptance scenarios
tests.procedure: Import sentence_stats from textstats. Call sentence_stats(''), sentence_stats('   \t\n '), and check isinstance(sentence_stats('')[1], float). Then call sentence_stats(None), sentence_stats(123), sentence_stats(b'a.').
tests.expected: The first two calls return (0, 0.0); the second value of sentence_stats('') is a float instance; the last three calls each raise TypeError.
